title: The whole rhythm
text:
Two squads. One small battlefield. Four rounds, called turning points. A first game may stop after two.

You move one model, then your opponent moves one, and so on until everyone has acted. That is the whole rhythm. Everything else is detail, and I am very good at detail.

title: Read your card
text:
Pick up one of your operatives' cards. Find four things: APL, which is how many actions it gets. Move. Save. Wounds. Say them aloud.

Now find a weapon. Atk is how many dice you roll. Hit is the number you need on each. Dmg is two numbers: normal damage, then critical.

title: Set up the terrain
text:
Place the terrain the way your mission's map shows. Yes, all of it.

Kill Team on an empty table is a shooting gallery, and nobody enjoys being the gallery.

title: Objectives
text:
Place the objective markers where the map shows.

Whoever has more APL within one inch of a marker controls it. Add up every operative that close.

That inch is the most important inch in the game. Measure it.

title: Roll off for drop zones
text:
Each of you roll one die. The higher roll picks a drop zone. Your mission's map shows where they are.

The other player takes the one that is left. I trust nobody is surprised.

title: Deploy
text:
Starting with the winner, take turns placing a third of your operatives at a time.

Every model starts with a Conceal order, the hidden one. Put the token beside it.

Then count each side's operatives. I will ask for the numbers next.

title: Your primary op
text:
One last secret. There are three ways to score: the Crit Op on the mission card, your Tac Op if you are using them, and the Kill Op.

Each of you privately picks one as your primary. At the end you get a bonus for it.

Write it down. Do not show it. Do not forget it.

title: The Strategy phase
text:
First, initiative. Both roll a die and the higher roll has it. Tell me who.

Second, command points. You each start with two and gain one now.

Third, flip every operative to Ready. Fourth, ploys, which we skip in a first game. Experts spend command points here. Tonight, hold them for re-rolls.

title: Your first activation
text:
Whoever has the initiative picks one operative and chooses its order: Conceal to stay hidden, Engage to act. Then spend its action points, one at a time.

When it is done, flip it to Expended and press the button. Then your opponent activates one.

Tell me when something shoots, charges, fights or is hurt. I explain each once.

title: Moving
text:
Reposition moves up to the Move number. Dash moves up to three inches more, and costs another action point. Measure from the edge of the base.

An operative on Conceal, in cover, cannot be shot at all. That is why the first round of Kill Team looks like a lot of hiding. It is.

title: Conceal or Engage
text:
Engage: the operative can do anything, shooting and charging included. It can also be shot by anything that sees it.

Conceal: no shooting, no charging. In return, while it is in cover it cannot be shot.

My rule of thumb: Conceal to get there, Engage to do something.

title: Shooting
text:
You need an Engage order, a target you can see, and none of your own operatives within an inch of it.

Roll your Atk dice. Sixes are critical, ones fail, the rest succeed at or above Hit. The defender rolls three dice against Save. In cover, one may be kept as a free success.

title: Blocking
text:
The defender now spends successes to cancel yours.

A normal stops a normal. Two normals stop a critical. A critical stops anything.

What survives is damage: the first Dmg number for each normal, the second for each critical. Take it off the target's wounds.

title: Charging
text:
A charge is a move of up to Move plus two inches that ends within an inch of an enemy. It needs an Engage order, and it cannot be combined with any other move in the same activation.

Once there, the two are engaged. Neither may simply walk away. Leaving is a Fall Back, and costs two action points.

title: Fighting
text:
Pick an enemy within an inch. Each of you picks a melee weapon and rolls its Atk dice.

Then take turns, attacker first, spending one success at a time. Strike, to deal that die's damage. Or parry, to cancel one of theirs.

Yes, they hit back. Melee in Kill Team is a conversation, not a monologue.

title: Injured
text:
Below half its starting wounds, an operative is injured: two inches less movement, and every Hit number one worse.

At no wounds it is incapacitated. Remove it, and tap Operative down.

An injured operative is still dangerous. Wounded things usually are.

title: Out of activations
text:
One of you has no ready operatives left. The other keeps activating, one at a time.

After each of those, the player with none left may counteract: one free action that costs one point, with an expended operative on Engage, moving no more than two inches.

title: Command points
text:
Command points buy ploys: strategy ploys in the Strategy phase, firefight ploys during activations. Each costs one, and each can be used once in a turning point. Your team's rules list them.

Re-rolling one attack or defence die is always on offer, for one point. Tap a number on my screen when you spend. Forgetting to spend them is the commonest leak.

title: End of turning point one
text:
Nothing scores from the Crit Op in the first turning point. By design, so nobody wins the game before it starts.

The Kill Op counts from now on, though. Open the score sheet, then carry on.

title: Strategy, again
text:
Initiative first. A tie goes to whoever did not have it last time.

Command points: the initiative holder gains one, the other gains two. A small kindness for going second.

Then flip every operative back to Ready.

title: Scoring
text:
Count control of each objective: most APL within an inch. Your Crit Op card says what that is worth.

Kill Op: count how many of the enemy's starting operatives are gone. Reach a kill grade, score a point.

Each of the three ops stops at six points. Update the sheet.

title: The last turning point
text:
After this scoring the game ends. Reveal your primary op. You add half of what you scored on it, rounded up, and never more than three.

The higher total prevails. Equal totals are a draw: the most honest result, and the least satisfying.

title: What to learn next
text:
Tac Ops and their archetypes. Strategy and firefight ploys. Equipment. Weapon keywords. Vantage points and climbing.

You now know enough to be dangerous. Next game I will say less and expect more.
